newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Crimea region elects pro-Kiev leader.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Crimea region elects pro-Kiev leader.

text.p: The parliament of Ukraine's Crimean peninsula elected a new pro-Kiev speaker on Thursday and cancelled a previous decision to sack the local government.
Deputies voted 54 to four to back Anatoly Gritsenko, 39, former head of eastern Crimea's local administration in Simferopol.
"The new leadership of the (Crimean) parliament consists of people who share and accept the policies of the Ukrainian president and parliament," Gritsenko told reporters after the vote.
"Relations between Simferopol and Kiev should be built on cooperation and mutual understanding," he said, adding that he would strictly obey Ukraine's constitution and laws.

The region of 2.7 million people, two-thirds of them ethnic Russians, was part of Russia for more than two centuries until Kremlin leader Nikita Khrushchev gave it to Ukraine, then a Soviet republic, as "gift" in 1954.

Last month the Crimean parliament voted to oust local Prime Minister Arkady Demidenko, who called the decision unconstitutional. After Thursday's vote Demidenko and his government, also viewed as loyal to Kiev, will remain in office.
